hs_stages.title: Zoning and building permits
hs_stages.lede: R and AF lots around Sandpoint are not the same. Extra dwellings, shops, and a tiny home each have a path — or they do not.
info: Look up zoning on the county map, not the listing adjective.
A building permit is the county (or the city if you are inside one). Bring the parcel number to the counter.
Owner-builder has limits. Electrical, plumbing, septic, and well are licensed trades.

hs_stages.title: Water and well permits
hs_stages.lede: Rural Bonner is wells. The log and a pump test tell you whether a house makes it through August.
info: Pull an IDWR well log for the parcel. A listing that says the area is good is not a log.
Four GPM can run a house; storage helps. Stock and irrigation want more, and irrigation is a water right.
A water test and a pump test during inspection are cheap compared to a dry well.

hs_stages.lede: Off city sewer, you are buying a septic system. Creek lots and a high water table can turn a gravity field into a mound.
info: Panhandle Health keeps septic records by section. Start with the parcel number from the assessor.
A finaled permit and room for a replacement field are the deal, not a tank lid in the grass.
Drainfields want about 100 feet from wells, and setback from creek or lake. New permit fee in the 2026 guidelines: $1,250.

hs_stages.lede: A rural parcel does not automatically get a mailbox. You need an address from the county, then a box the carrier will actually stop at.

Cluster boxes are common on private spurs. A roadside box needs a pull-out the plow will not bury.
The UPS Store in Sandpoint rents boxes if the carrier will not come up your road yet.
